subject: ventures/ai-bookkeeper
professional: a CPA / QuickBooks ProAdvisor who closes books for sole proprietors and small businesses from bank and card statements; first checks: do transfers and card payments stay out of expenses, does the ledger balance and tie to the statement's closing balance, are dates read the right way round, and do the SE-tax and estimated-tax worksheets match the IRS forms

evidence.correctness: Sampled engines: bank.mjs (CSV reader), engine.mjs (import, transfer pairing, journal), ledger.mjs, categorize.mjs, taxforms.mjs, estimatedtax.mjs, reconcile.mjs, plus the page. Ran them with hand-built inputs (scratchpad t1.mjs, t2.mjs, t3.mjs). Recomputed by hand: (1) a 5-line checking CSV with a running balance (1000.00 - 12.50 - 300.00 - 54.99 - 23.10 = 609.41) agrees with the tool's close check 'Checking agrees with the statement's closing balance of 609.41', the 300.00 card payment pairs into one transfer (not an expense), card account balance 300.00 - 45.67 = 254.33 and the trial balance (debits = credits = 1,000.00) match; parenthesised '(12.50)' read as -1250 cents; (2) Schedule SE on 100,000 profit: 92.35% = 92,350.00; social security 12.4% = 11,451.40; Medicare 2.9% = 2,678.15; total 14,129.55; half 7,064.78: all match selfEmployment(); on 200,000 the 184,500 wage base caps SS at 22,878.00 and Medicare is 184,700 x 2.9% = 5,356.30: both match; (3) 2026 single-filer federal estimate on 100,000 profit by hand: AGI 100,000 - 7,064.78 = 92,935.22, less 16,100 standard = 76,835.22, QBI 20% = 15,367.04, taxable 61,468.18, tax 1,240 + 4,560 + 22% x 11,068.18 = 8,235.00, plus SE tax = 22,364.55; estimatedTax() returns taxable 6,146,818 cents, income tax 823,500, total 2,236,455: all match (brackets and standard deduction are from the auditor's recollection of Rev. Proc. 2025-32, consistent with the file; irs.gov not fetched); (4) the page in headless Chrome: example loaded, every suggestion accepted, the 36 remaining lines filed by hand, balance sheet Checking = 10,947.46 as README claims. Wrong or weak outputs found: none wrong in these runs; 'SQ *BLUE BOTTLE 0412 OAKLAND CA' gets no suggestion (queue, not an error); a two-row file '03/04/2026, 04/05/2026' is read month-first with no warning in problems (the ambiguity note only fires for larger all-ambiguous files).
evidence.completeness: Checked against README/llms.txt/page: CSV import with parentheses and running balance (worked); transfer pairing (worked); review queue accept/ file (worked in Chrome); trial balance, P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, ratios (reports keys present, balanced true); close checks reconcile (worked); reconcile hints (read, covered by tests); SE tax and estimated tax (worked, hand-matched); CSV-injection guard on journal export ('=cmd|...' exported as '=cmd... with leading apostrophe, worked); eval/benchmark.mjs (runs, see claims for drift); eval/*.test.mjs 550/550 pass. Not exercised end to end by me: BAI2, N43, CFONB, MT940/CAMT, OCR/PDF, QuickBooks Desktop IIF, AI layer (no key or local model; README itself says AI accuracy is not measured), payroll, accruals. No stubs found in sampled files. Stage in VENTURE.yaml is 'prototype' and README says 'not yet measured' for real bank exports and AI accuracy, which is honest.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in ventures/ai-bookkeeper (run in background, ~54 s): 2371 tests, 2371 pass, 0 fail. `node --test eval/*.test.mjs`: 550 pass, 0 fail. Two seeded mutations, each reverted with git checkout (git status on the venture clean afterwards): (A) engine.mjs pairTransfers `gap <= days` -> `gap < days` (the documented 'within 5 days' boundary): 2371/2371 still pass, NOT caught; (B) categorize.mjs memory confidence `n / (total + 0.5)` -> `n / (total + 0.3)`: 2 tests failed ('payee memory returns the most frequent account, not the runner-up'; 'a confirmed choice is remembered: the payee posts itself after three'), caught. The suite is broad (property, metamorphic, fuzz, round-trip tests, hostile-input tests), but at least one boundary in a core engine is untested. Test files named probe5..probe30.test.mjs and gaps4/gaps5 do not say what they cover.
evidence.craft: Read ledger.mjs (integer cents throughout, validateEntry rejects unbalanced entries, pure functions), reconcile.mjs, the importStatement/pairTransfers/analyze parts of engine.mjs, suggest() in categorize.mjs, the head of estimatedtax.mjs. Good: integer cents, immutable-style books (clone), explicit problems list instead of throwing on bad rows, layers can be switched off for ablation, every result carries a reason. Defects: very dense one-line functions (ledger.mjs profitAndLoss/balanceSheet; engine.mjs importStatement lines), bank.mjs is 1,254 lines with format sniffing in one module, a 28k-line venture with opaque test names (probe5..probe30, gaps4, gaps5) and about 50 eval/probe*.mjs scripts committed, a binary ledger-1.0.1 .whl in the folder, estimatedtax.mjs header comment is a run-on of dated check notes. estimatedTax payment plan marks all four 2026 dates 'due' when run in November without an as-of date.
evidence.claims: Backed: disclaimer and 'no warranty ... estimates' text (index.html:454, 'Not accounting or tax advice' index.html:70); 'nothing uploaded' (Playwright: zero non-localhost requests, no console errors, no horizontal scroll at 390 px); 'Checking agrees with the statement's closing balance of $10,947.46' (reproduced); 'two bank accounts equal and opposite within 5 days pair' (works; boundary untested); SE-tax wage bases and 2026 brackets (match my hand calc and my recollection). Not backed or stale: (1) README's learning-curve table no longer matches the code: README month 01 reads 133/133 (100.0%) right with 42.1% no suggestion; `node eval/benchmark.mjs --seeds 5` today prints 164/174 (94.3%) with 25.5% no suggestion, and months 4-12 60.0% posted alone / 0.1% wrong versus README's 60.1% / '1 of 1,300'; (2) llms.txt:5 says the tool 'does not do payroll, sales tax filings' while llms.txt:56 and README document payroll.mjs and salestaxreturn.mjs; (3) llms.txt and the sitemap point to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address (53 occurrences in llms.txt, sitemap.xml and index.html) instead of marisstella.app; (4) README 'Tests: node --test ventures/ai-bookkeeper/*.test.mjs' omits the 550 tests under eval/. The README is candid about synthetic data and unmeasured AI accuracy, which keeps this from a 1.
evidence.fitness: Walked a sole proprietor's month: paste a bank CSV (parenthesised debit, running balance) and a card CSV, accept suggestions, file the rest, read the P&L and balance sheet, tie to the statement (worked in Chrome and via analyze()), export a QBO journal (safe against formula injection). Transfers and card payments stay out of expenses, which is the first mistake a CPA looks for. Gaps a bookkeeper would hit: first-month queue is large (139 of 145 example lines wait; 36 still had no suggestion after 'accept at 0'), payroll and GUSTO lines land in a generic expense (6150) unless payroll import is used, no bank feeds, and a two-row ambiguous-date file is silently read month-first. The core job finishes; the tool does not pretend to replace a CPA's year-end review.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard small-business practice (cash-basis bookkeeping from bank lines, transfers netted, owner draws/contributions to equity, trial balance that balances, reconcile to statement closing balance) and against IRS Schedule SE (92.35%, 12.4% to the wage base, 2.9%, half deductible) and the Form 1040 flow (standard deduction, QBI 20% limited by taxable income, bracket tax): all agree in my recomputation. Departures a practitioner would raise: the QBI treatment is simplified (documented), the 2026 bracket and wage-base figures were checked by me only against recollection (irs.gov and ssa.gov not fetched this round), the estimated-tax plan splits the safe harbour into four equal payments without an as-of default, accrual is partial (documents are optional), and the review queue defaults send bank-category-less deposits to Sales at 0.7 confidence, which is a suggestion only and never posts alone (consistent with the README's 'only a rule or memory posts itself').

defects.what: Seeded mutation of the documented 5-day transfer window (`gap <= days` -> `gap < days`) passed all 2371 tests: the boundary of transfer pairing is untested, and a wrong boundary would leave a card payment in the review queue or as an expense.

README learning-curve table is stale against the code: month 01 shows 133/133 (100.0%) correct with 42.1% no suggestion, but `node eval/benchmark.mjs --seeds 5` now prints 164/174 (94.3%) with 25.5% no suggestion; months 4-12 'posted alone' is 60.0%, not 60.1%. The text also cites the old numbers ('month 1's 100% (133 of 133)').

llms.txt tells LLM readers the tool 'does not do payroll, sales tax filings', contradicting llms.txt line 56, README and payroll.mjs / salestaxreturn.mjs; its page links and sitemap point at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host (53 occurrences) instead of https://marisstella.app/ai-bookkeeper/.

A short all-ambiguous date file (two rows, 03/04/2026 and 04/05/2026) is read month-first with an empty problems list: no warning that day-first was possible, so a UK file lands in the wrong months silently. Larger all-ambiguous files do warn (bank.mjs:920).
estimatedTax() run without an as-of date in November 2026 reports all four 2026 installments (April, June, September, January) as 'due' with equal amounts, instead of marking the past ones.

Opaque test and probe names (probe5..probe30.test.mjs, gaps4/gaps5.test.mjs, about 50 eval/probe*.mjs scripts), dense one-line functions in ledger.mjs and engine.mjs, and a committed binary ledger-1.0.1 wheel make the 28k-line venture hard to review.

verdict: A genuinely deep, mostly correct tool that I could break only at the edges. Run against hand-built input it was right every time: a 5-line statement ties to its 609.41 closing balance with the card payment paired as a transfer, Schedule SE on 100,000 and 200,000 matches the form line by line, a 2026 single-filer estimate (taxable 61,468.18, total 22,364.55) matches my own computation, and the page in Chrome reproduces the README's 10,947.46 checking balance with no console errors, no external requests and no horizontal scroll at 390 px. 2371 tests plus 550 eval tests pass, and they caught a seeded change to the memory-confidence formula, but a seeded change to the 5-day transfer boundary went unnoticed. It falls short of the bar on claims: the README's learning-curve table no longer matches what the benchmark prints (94.3%, not 100%, in month 1), and llms.txt says the tool does not do payroll or sales-tax filings while documenting both, and points to the retired github.io host. Correctness 3, verification 3, claims 2: finished by its own README, not at the bar until the claims are brought back in line. I did not exercise the AI layer, the non-CSV bank formats, payroll or accruals end to end, and the tax tables were checked against recollection, not the IRS text, this round.
